  - text: 01 / CASE FILE
  - heading "What is actually confirmed" [level=2]
  - paragraph: The strongest claims are backed by live reads of OpenSea, Blockscout, Helixa, plus indexed project documentation and the mint-announcement Space recap.

  - article:
    - text: THE CONCEPT
    - heading "The image is the behavioral schema" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Eyes, mouth, hair, clothing, class, specialization, risk, and autonomy are not just visual metadata. The launch concept says each trait maps to a personality characteristic that changes how the AI agent behaves. A 721T metadata layer and ERC-8004 adapter are meant to keep NFT ownership, agent identity, and reputation bound together.
    - text: "Source:"
    - link "Mint Space recap ↗":
      - /url: https://recapspaces.com/quigleynft/humans-in-the-loop-loopers-nft-mint-announcement/

  - text: 02 / LAUNCH
  - heading "A delay, then a sellout" [level=2]
  - paragraph: "The launch record is unusually candid: the team postponed during its own announcement Space rather than ship art that had not passed QA."
  - article:
    - text: THURSDAY · SEP 3, 2026
    - strong: Mint announcement Space
    - paragraph: Quigley hosted a 1h 43m “humans in the loop” Space with roughly eight speakers. The team outlined trait-to-personality agents, 721T, ERC-8004 binding, and a holder-run “decentralized swarm.”
    - text: DURING THE SPACE
    - strong: Launch postponed
    - paragraph: Quigley said the final art-generation QA agent stopped responding after being pushed too hard. The mint was delayed rather than released unfinished.
    - text: ANNOUNCED TERMS
    - strong: 0.0037 ETH allowlist · 0.0077 ETH public
    - paragraph: The plan was a seven-day Base mint with staggered reveal. Timing remained open, possibly the next morning.
    - text: BY SEP 20, 2026
    - strong: 7,777 onchain supply
    - paragraph: Blockscout showed the full supply. OpenSea labeled the collection “SEP 2026,” confirming the broad window but not the exact live date or mint-out time.
    - text: "Sources:"
    - link "Space recap ↗":
      - /url: https://recapspaces.com/quigleynft/humans-in-the-loop-loopers-nft-mint-announcement/
    - text: ·

  - complementary:
    - text: WHY IT MATTERS
    - heading "Reputation before autonomy" [level=3]
    - paragraph: The stated model was not “full permissions on day one.” Agents would earn permission to trade, launch tokens, and build apps as reputation grew. That makes the identity and scoring layer operational, not decorative.
    - text: "Source:"
    - link "Space recap ↗":
      - /url: https://recapspaces.com/quigleynft/humans-in-the-loop-loopers-nft-mint-announcement/

  - text: 04 / ANOMALY
  - heading "The 45-holder mystery is an indexer problem" [level=2]
  - paragraph: Two public views appeared to disagree by 28×. The transfer count explains why.
  - text: BLOCKSCOUT HOLDER TAB 45 and 0 indexed token transfers OPENSEA UNIQUE OWNERS 1,256 with active listings and sales
  - strong: "Resolution:"
  - text: Blockscout’s holder tab is a partial sample. Its transfer index shows zero events for this contract, despite full supply and marketplace activity. The largest address Blockscout does list holds only 50 tokens (0.64%), which argues against a hidden treasury or distributor controlling the missing supply. For distribution, use OpenSea’s 1,256 unique-owner count from this snapshot.
  - article:
    - text: WHAT THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS
    - heading "Partial event indexing" [level=3]
    - paragraph: The 721T implementation may not emit the standard events Blockscout’s pipeline parses, or the indexing is otherwise incomplete. The exact technical cause was not proven, so this remains a mechanism-level hypothesis—not a contract audit finding.
    - text: "Source:"
    - link "Blockscout live read ↗":
      - /url: https://base.blockscout.com/token/0x1649CD37f4748807b4882FC48765bA0B2aFfa94a
  - article:
    - text: TOP LISTED HOLDER 50 tokens · 0.64%
    - paragraph: Next visible balances included 20 and 14, then many at 10, 9, 8, and 6.
